results.result: The authors identified a neuronal cluster defined by gsc2 expression that is distinct from and located anterior to rln3a neurons in the zebrafish NI, positioned dorsal to the IPN.
results.evaluation: All reviewers accepted the identification and anatomical characterization of gsc2 neurons as a distinct population. The editor noted 'important finding on the anatomical connectivity' and reviewers praised the 'genetic approach that enabled the authors to characterize many different features of the two genetically targeted populations' without questioning the basic anatomical claims.

results.result: The authors characterized neuropeptide expression in the zebrafish NI, finding that gsc2 neurons do not express neuropeptides (cckb, nmbb, nts), while rln3a and nmbb neurons are intermingled in the NI with some co-expression, and cckb neurons form a separate posterior population.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the neuropeptide expression characterization. One reviewer noted the study 'relies on a series of rigorous experimental approaches including molecular genetic, neuroanatomical, functional and behavioral analysis' and that 'technical weaknesses present in the first version of the manuscript have largely been addressed in the present revision,' indicating acceptance of these molecular findings.

results.result: The authors generated two transgenic knock-in lines, Tg(gsc2:QF2)c721 and Tg(rln3a:QF2, he1.1:YFP)c836, that recapitulate endogenous expression patterns of gsc2 and rln3a at both larval and adult stages.
results.evaluation: Multiple reviewers explicitly praised the transgenic lines. One reviewer stated 'the authors have made two beautiful knock-in lines that recapitulate endogenous expression pattern of gsc2 and rln3a which will be a powerful tool' and another noted 'the resources generated including the two knock-in transgenic reporter lines will be of great value for the zebrafish neurobiology community.' No concerns were raised about the fidelity of these lines.

results.result: The authors demonstrated that both gsc2 and rln3a neurons in the NI are predominantly GABAergic (approximately 80% co-expression with GABAergic markers), with similar neurotransmitter identity across neuroanatomical locations for rln3a neurons.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not question the neurotransmitter identity findings. One reviewer noted 'experiments are well done, data are high quality and most claims are well supported' and another stated 'technical weaknesses present in the first version of the manuscript have largely been addressed,' suggesting acceptance of these characterization data.

results.result: The authors showed that gsc2 and rln3a NI neurons have widely divergent and largely non-overlapping projection patterns, with gsc2 neurons projecting more extensively to cerebellum, IPN, raphe, diencephalon, and hypothalamus, while rln3a NI neurons project exclusively to the IPN.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed the projection pattern findings. One reviewer stated the authors 'show that the gsc2+ and rln3a+ NI neurons show divergent projection patterns' and another noted they 'present convincing evidence that these cells have different patterns of connectivity.' The editor highlighted 'important finding on the anatomical connectivity' without raising concerns about the projection data.

results.result: The authors demonstrated that gsc2 and rln3a neurons innervate distinct subregions of the IPN, with gsc2 neurons terminating at the ventral IPN along the midline neuropil and rln3a neurons terminating at the dorsal IPN.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the IPN innervation patterns but raised a caveat about interpretation. One reviewer noted 'the data very clearly show different patterns of neurites for gsc2 and rln3a neurons in the IPN and the authors interpret these are being axonal arbors. However, they do not rule out the possibility that some of the processes might be dendritic in nature.' Despite this interpretive note, the basic finding of distinct IPN subregion innervation was not challenged.

results.result: The authors showed that activation of the dHb-IPN axis increases activity in gsc2 neurons but not in rln3a neurons, indicating differential afferent input between these populations.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the optogenetic mapping findings. One reviewer noted the study includes 'imaging and manipulations of the genetically targeted populations of neurons' and another stated 'experiments are well done, data are high quality.' However, one reviewer commented that 'the anatomical study revealed the connections from the NI to the IPN, while the optogenetic mapping experiments investigate the other way around,' suggesting the circuit understanding could be more integrated but not disputing the findings themselves.

results.result: The authors demonstrated that gsc2 and rln3a neurons differ in their spontaneous activity and response to electric shock, with gsc2 neurons showing little spontaneous activity but robust shock responses, while rln3a neurons exhibit spontaneous fluctuations and shorter-duration shock responses.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the calcium imaging findings but noted the dichotomy is not absolute. One reviewer stated 'although the gsc2 and rln3a populations show differences in calcium activity, there is not as clear a dichotomy as stated in the abstract. For example, both populations clearly respond to electric shocks, albeit with different response time courses.' This indicates the findings are supported but the interpretation of complete functional separation was questioned.

results.result: The authors showed that ablation of rln3a NI neurons (but not gsc2 or rln3a PAG neurons) causes hyperactivity in zebrafish larvae, with increased swimming distance, longer activity phases, and increased turning behavior, indicating that rln3a NI neurons regulate locomotor activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the behavioral findings without challenge. One reviewer noted the authors 'present convincing evidence that these cells have different patterns of connectivity, calcium activity and effects on behavior' and the editor stated the work presents 'important finding on the anatomical connectivity and functional roles.' The selective effect of rln3a NI neuron ablation on locomotion was not disputed.

results.result: The authors found that loss of either NI rln3a or gsc2 neurons was not sufficient to alter hyperactivity normally observed in zebrafish larvae post-shock.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge this negative finding. The overall behavioral characterization was accepted as part of the comprehensive functional analysis, with one reviewer noting 'experiments are well done, data are high quality and most claims are well supported.'

results.result: The authors concluded that the anatomical location, neurotransmitter phenotype, and connectivity of gsc2 and rln3a neurons are consistent with NI identity, supporting that the zebrafish griseum centrale is analogous to the mammalian NI, and that these adjacent populations have distinct properties.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accepted the overall conclusion about NI identity and functional diversity. The editor noted this presents 'important finding on the anatomical connectivity and functional roles of the previously uncharacterized neuronal populations in the nucleus incertus' and one reviewer stated the findings 'will be valuable in support of future endeavors' to understand NI function. The comparative anatomy claim was not challenged.

results.result: The authors suggested conservation of NI cell types and their organization from fish to mammals based on similarities in neuropeptide expression patterns.
results.evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the evolutionary conservation argument. One reviewer noted the work will 'inspire further studies of the NI in other model systems,' implicitly accepting the cross-species relevance of the findings.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on transgenic line validation (C65-C68). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers found the knock-in lines faithfully reproduce endogenous expression patterns. Peer reviewers explicitly praised these as 'beautiful knock-in lines' and 'powerful tools'.

Perfect agreement on neurotransmitter identity characterization (C76-C83). Both evaluations accepted the glutamatergic/GABAergic classification based on double-labeling experiments. Peer reviewers noted experiments are 'well done' with 'high quality' data.

Perfect agreement on projection patterns (C4, C7, C84-C96). Both evaluations strongly supported the divergent projection patterns of gsc2 and rln3a neurons. Peer reviewers presented 'convincing evidence' for different connectivity patterns, and editor highlighted this as an 'important finding'.

Agreement on optogenetic mapping findings (C103-C105, C155). Both accepted the differential IPN responses to gsc2 vs rln3a activation. Peer reviewers noted one interpretive concern about circuit directionality but did not dispute the findings themselves.

Agreement on calcium imaging data (C5, C9-C10, C107-C111, C156) but with nuanced interpretation differences. OpenEval emphasized distinct activity patterns with statistical support. Peer reviewers accepted findings but noted the dichotomy is 'not as clear' as stated in abstract, since both populations respond to shocks albeit differently.

Strong agreement on behavioral findings (C6, C11, C115-C117, C135-C141, C157). Both evaluations supported the selective effect of rln3a NI neuron ablation on locomotion. Peer reviewers found 'convincing evidence' for behavioral differences without challenge.

Agreement on negative finding regarding post-shock hyperactivity (C126). Both evaluations accepted that neither neuronal population is required for immediate locomotor response to aversive stimuli. Peer reviewers did not challenge this as part of comprehensive behavioral analysis.

Agreement on overall NI identity and functional diversity conclusions (C151-C154). Both evaluations supported the characterization of these neurons as nucleus incertus and the evolutionary conservation argument. Editor noted 'important finding' on previously uncharacterized NI populations.

Agreement on IPN innervation patterns (C8, C98-C101, C161) with interpretive caveat. OpenEval supported distinct IPN subregion innervation based on anatomical data. Peer reviewers accepted the different patterns but noted processes might be dendritic rather than purely axonal, though this did not challenge the basic finding.

Agreement on gsc2 neuron identification and anatomical characterization (C3, C52-C54). OpenEval found strong support from in situ hybridization. Peer reviewers accepted without question, praising the 'genetic approach' and noting 'important finding on anatomical connectivity'. OpenEval also evaluated C57-C58 which peer review grouped with neuropeptide claims.

Agreement on neuropeptide expression patterns (C55-C56, C59-C64). OpenEval supported claims with in situ hybridization data. Peer reviewers accepted molecular findings as part of 'rigorous experimental approaches' without challenge. Peer review also included evolutionary conservation claims (C128-C131) not in this OpenEval result.

Partial overlap on evolutionary conservation of NI cell types (C128-C131). OpenEval R12 evaluated these claims as supported by in situ data and literature comparisons, though noted direct comparative studies would strengthen conclusions. Peer R2 accepted these as part of overall molecular characterization.

Agreement on evolutionary conservation argument (C132). OpenEval supported parallel organization across species based on molecular data and literature. Peer reviewers accepted cross-species relevance, noting work will 'inspire further studies of the NI in other model systems'.

OpenEval identified speculative claims about developmental differences and mechanisms (C118, C121, C148) as UNCERTAIN, requiring additional studies for full support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific speculative interpretations.

These represent established knowledge providing context rather than novel findings. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate background claims.
